notes: This descriptor documents the currently active packaged PRoot asset.
Active runtime is the KF lifecycle telemetry build from the Termux PRoot fork.
PRoot emits low-cost fork/clone/vfork/exec/exit/signal JSONL events to KF_PROOT_TELEMETRY_PATH.

Lifecycle v3 additionally exports telemetrySessionId, prootStartMs, processGroupId, sessionId, exitCode, signal, and scans the full exec envp for whitelisted KF_RUNTIME_ID/KF_UNIT_ID values when present.
Lifecycle v4 additionally projects high-value /proc/<pid> files through KF_PROCFS_PROJECTION_ROOT so Ubuntu process queries can consume PRoot event-backed facts without broad rescans.

Lifecycle v5 additionally keeps inherited command/runtime identity on fork/clone/vfork events and preserves last command identity on exit/signal events; runtime-process-table.tsv exposes started_at_ms.
Lifecycle v6 additionally rotates the raw telemetry JSONL at 8 MiB with three archives; KF retains all running tracees and bounds terminal live-table history to 5000 entries or 7 days.
Lifecycle v7 keeps procfs projection for normal Ubuntu commands but lets kf-resource-sampler bypass stat/statm projection and update runtime-process-table resource columns.
Lifecycle v8 additionally lets standard resource-view commands such as ps aux and top bypass stat/statm projection while refreshing runtime-process-table resource columns on read.
Lifecycle v9 emits eventSeq, lifecycleSeq, parentLifecycleSeq, and startTimeTicks, and maintains a per-PRoot active tracee registry for cold-start and event-gap reconciliation.
Lifecycle v10 fixes active-registry JSON framing so native registry snapshots can be parsed during cold-start and event-gap reconciliation.
Lifecycle v11 retries identity capture for the initial tracee at its first event, preventing owner shutdown from falling back to shared Android process groups.
Lifecycle v12 atomically retires empty active-registry sessions, keeping registry cost proportional to current live PRoot sessions instead of accumulated history.
PRoot is a fact source only; Android/KF remains the policy and execution authority.
Stock PRoot remains packaged as a no-telemetry fallback.
Legacy termux-baseline remains packaged only as quarantined historical metadata.
Runtime migration preserves containers, shared workspace, containers.json, and terminal-sessions.json while rewriting APK-owned runtime assets.
